app.name: Color Vision Detective
app.tagline: A 3-minute color vision screening, plus tools that use your result

disclaimer.notDiagnosis: This test is not a medical diagnosis. Results are a screening estimate, used to tune color tools for you.
disclaimer.seeDoctor: If you think your color vision may be different, please see an eye doctor for a professional exam.
disclaimer.howItWorks: You'll see patterns made of colored dots. Find the square that looks different. It takes about 3 minutes (60–75 questions).

disclaimer.localOnly: Your result is stored only on this device and is never uploaded.

prep.distance.tablet: Hold it about 40–50 cm from your eyes.
prep.distance.desktop: Sit about 50–60 cm (roughly an arm's length) from the screen.

prep.brightnessHint.tablet: Drag the brightness slider all the way up
prep.brightnessHint.desktop: Use the brightness keys or display settings; plug a laptop into power so it doesn't dim

prep.nightModeHint.tablet: iPad: long-press brightness in Control Center; Android: Quick Settings
prep.nightModeHint.desktop: macOS: System Settings → Displays → Night Shift; Windows: Settings → Display → Night light
prep.trueTone: True Tone / eye comfort mode is off
prep.trueToneHint.phone: iOS: Settings → Display & Brightness; Android: Display settings
prep.trueToneHint.tablet: iPad: Settings → Display & Brightness; Android: Display settings

settings.title: Settings
settings.dataBody: Your test results and preferences are stored only in this browser (localStorage). No cookies, no accounts, no analytics. Images you fix are processed in memory and are never saved or uploaded.

settings.storageMemory: Storage status: not saving — data will be lost when you close the page.

settings.cleared: All local data has been cleared.
settings.privacy1: Where data lives: only in this browser on this device. Other people using their own devices have their own separate results.
settings.privacy2: What the server sees: nothing. It only serves static files and receives no results or images.
settings.privacy3: Moving devices: use a backup file or a parameter link. The link keeps your result after the #, which is never sent to a server.
settings.privacy4: How to delete: use the button above, or clear this site's data in your browser settings.
settings.about: Color Vision Detective is a screening tool, not a medical diagnosis.

fixer.mode.label: Fix for

fixer.using.none: No test result yet. Pick a type below, or take the 3-minute test for better results.

fixer.using.everyoneTritan: Covers red-type, green-type and blue-yellow color blindness at full strength.

guide.title: User guide
guide.lead: How to get a reliable result and make the most of the Chart Fixer and Color Radar.
guide.about.title: What this app is
guide.about.1: Color Vision Detective is a browser-based screening tool with three parts: a 3-minute color vision test, a Chart Fixer for images, and Color Radar for the world around you.
guide.about.2: The test estimates the type of color vision difference (red-type / protan, green-type / deutan, blue-yellow / tritan), how strong it is, and how confident the estimate is. It is not a medical diagnosis: phone and computer screens aren't calibrated. If you think your color vision may be different, see an eye doctor.
guide.about.3: Everything runs on your device. Nothing you do here is uploaded.
guide.prepare.title: Before the test
guide.prepare.1: Turn screen brightness all the way up.
guide.prepare.2: Turn off Night Shift / night mode and True Tone / eye-comfort modes. They tint the screen and shift the test colors.
guide.prepare.3: Avoid strong colored lighting. Ordinary indoor light or daylight is best; avoid glare and reflections on the screen.
guide.prepare.4: Any device with a color screen works: phone, tablet or computer. Hold a phone about 30–40 cm and a tablet about 40–50 cm from your eyes, or sit about 50–60 cm from a computer screen. The test detects the kind of device and reminds you.
guide.prepare.5: The "Before you start" screen walks you through these checks.
guide.test.title: Taking the test
guide.test.1: Each question shows four squares made of colored dots. Tap the one that looks different. The dots vary in brightness on purpose, so look for a difference in color, not lightness.
guide.test.2: Three practice rounds come first and are not scored. The test itself takes about 3 minutes (60–75 questions) and gets harder as you answer correctly.
guide.test.3: If you really can't see a difference, tap Can't tell instead of guessing.
guide.test.4: Answer at your natural pace. Answers that come much more slowly than your own usual pace are treated as likely guesses and count less. If the deciding answers were mostly slow, the result says the red/green type is unclear instead of guessing it.
guide.test.5: Now and then an easy check question appears to make sure the test has your attention.
guide.test.6: The language switch is hidden during the test, because switching would restart it.
guide.results.title: Reading your result
guide.results.1: Type: typical color vision, red-type (protan), green-type (deutan), blue-yellow (tritan), or red-green with the type unclear.
guide.results.2: Level (mild, moderate, severe) and a continuous severity from 0 to 100%, which the Chart Fixer and Color Radar use to tune themselves to you.
guide.results.3: Confidence (low, medium, high) drops after missed check questions, too few reliable answers, or many slow answers. If it's low, retest in better conditions.
guide.results.4: Per-axis thresholds show how large a color difference you needed on each axis, and the comparison slider estimates how the world may look to you.
guide.results.5: Retaking the test replaces your current result; the previous one is kept in history.
guide.fixer.title: Chart Fixer
guide.fixer.1: Upload, drop or paste a chart, map or diagram (PNG, JPG or WebP), or try one of the samples.
guide.fixer.2: For me uses your test result. For everyone makes the chart friendly for common types of color blindness, which is good for sharing.
guide.fixer.3: Only colors that are hard to tell apart are changed. Compare before and after, use Show how I see it, lock colors you want to keep, adjust the strength, and download a PNG.
guide.fixer.4: Without a test result you can pick a type manually.
guide.radar.title: Color Radar
guide.radar.1: Color Radar works on your live camera, or on an uploaded photo. Allow camera access when asked; on a computer without a camera, use Image to upload a photo.
guide.radar.2: Highlight: tap a color. Similar areas stay in color with a white outline and everything else turns grey. Use Tolerance to widen or narrow the match, and Clear color to stop.
guide.radar.3: Separate: shifts colors that are hard for you to tell apart so they stand out, tuned to your test result. Use Strength to adjust. With typical color vision there's nothing to enhance; when the red/green type is unclear it corrects for both.
guide.radar.4: Name: tap to move the crosshair; the color's name appears below it. Very dark or very bright scenes show a lighting warning.
guide.radar.5: Gestures: tap to pick a color or move the crosshair, press and hold to compare with the original picture, double-tap to freeze or resume (the Freeze button does the same).
guide.radar.6: The chip at the top right shows your type, level and confidence. Tap it to open Radar settings, where you can also set a type and severity manually for this session.
guide.share.title: Sharing and moving your result
guide.share.1: Your result is saved only in this browser. To use it in another browser or on another device, open My Results and copy the parameter link or download a backup file.
guide.share.2: Open the link on the other device, or paste it on the Import page, where backup files can be imported too. Importing replaces the result saved on that device.
guide.share.3: The link keeps your result after the #, which browsers never send to a server. It carries type, level, severity and confidence, but not per-axis details.
guide.devices.title: Using different devices
guide.devices.1: The test measures what this screen lets you see. Screens differ in color and brightness, so the same person can get a different severity on a phone and on a computer; the type is usually the same.
guide.devices.2: Each result records the kind of device it was tested on (shown as "Tested on a phone / tablet / computer"). You'll get a note when you retest or import a result from a different kind of device.
guide.devices.3: The Chart Fixer and Color Radar don't measure anything themselves; they only use your saved result. For the best fit, use a result from a device similar to the one you use them on.
guide.devices.4: Results live only in this browser. To move one to another device, use a parameter link or backup file from My Results, or take the test again on the new device.
guide.privacy.title: Privacy
guide.privacy.1: No accounts, cookies or analytics. Results and preferences stay in this browser's local storage.
guide.privacy.2: Camera frames and images are processed on your device and are never saved or uploaded.
guide.privacy.3: Delete everything with Settings → Clear all data on this device, or clear this site's data in your browser.
